37060-through-these-eyes-the-courageous-.title: Through These Eyes The Courageous Struggle To Find Meaning I
37060-through-these-eyes-the-courageous-.creator: Unknown
37060-through-these-eyes-the-courageous-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. THROUGH THESE EYES, written by Lauren A. Isaacson (10 Dec 1961 - 16 Jul 1986), is rare in several respects. At the age of twelve, she was diagnosed as having cancer of the stomach; leiomyosarcoma is a cancer prevalent in older women. She was accepted at the Mayo Clinic for research, and after a five year period was given a clean bill of health. During her sixth year following chemotherapy, she was diagnosed as suffering from the same cancer; it had invaded the liver.

arxiv-2105-00579.title: BackdooRL : Backdoor Attack against Competitive Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2105-00579.creator: Lun Wang, Zaynah Javed, Xian Wu, Wenbo Guo, Xinyu Xing, Dawn Song
arxiv-2105-00579.description: Abstract Recent research has confirmed the feasibility of backdoor attacks in deep reinforcement learning (RL) systems. However, the existing attacks require the ability to arbitrarily modify an agent’s observation, constraining the application scope to simple RL systems such as Atari games.

arxiv-2107-10693.title: Dark Twilight Joined with the Light of Dawn to Unveil the Reionization History
arxiv-2107-10693.creator: Daniela Paoletti, Dhiraj Kumar Hazra, Fabio Finelli, George F. Smoot
arxiv-2107-10693.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniela Paoletti, Dhiraj Kumar Hazra, Fabio Finelli, George F. Smoot. Improved measurement of the Cosmic Microwave Background polarization from Planck allows a detailed study of reionization beyond the average optical depth. The lower value of the optical depth disfavours an early onset and an early completion of reionization in favour of a redsfhit range where different astrophysical probes provide sensible information on the sources of reionization and the status of the intergalactic medium.

arxiv-2111-00675.title: Local two- and three-nucleon chiral interactions
arxiv-2111-00675.creator: Maria Piarulli, Rocco Schiavilla
arxiv-2111-00675.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Maria Piarulli, Rocco Schiavilla. Understanding the structure and reactions of nuclei from first principles has been a long-standing goal of nuclear physics. In this respect, few- and many-body systems provide a unique laboratory for studying nuclear interactions. In the past couple of decades, the modeling of nuclear interactions has progressed significantly owing, in particular, to the development of chiral effective field theory ( χ \chi EFT), a low-energy effective representation of quantum chromodynamics (QCD).

arxiv-2306-17174.title: Empowering NLG: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Informal Summarization in Online Domains
arxiv-2306-17174.creator: Zhi-Xuan Tai, Po-Chuan Chen
arxiv-2306-17174.description: Abstract We present an innovative approach to Natural Language Generation (NLG) that aims to enhance user experience and reduce the workload of human customer support agents. Specifically, our focus is on generating informal summaries for online articles and posts using an offline reinforcement learning method.

arxiv-2310-11847.title: On gravity unification in SL(2N,C)
arxiv-2310-11847.creator: gauge theories
arxiv-2310-11847.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by gauge theories. The local
SL(2N,C)
symmetry is shown to provide, when appropriately
constrained, a viable framework for a consistent unification of the known
elementary forces, including gravity. Such a covariant constraint implies
that an actual gauge field multiplet in the
SL(2N,C)
theory is ultimately
determined by the associated tetrad fields which not only specify the
geometric features of spacetime but also govern which local internal
symmetries are permissible within it.

arxiv-2310-18123.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Score-Matching: Causal Discovery and Generative Modeling
arxiv-2310-18123.creator: Zhenyu Zhu, Francesco Locatello, Volkan Cevher, † \dagger École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne Institute of Science, Technology Austria, † \dagger {zhenyu.zhu, volkan.cevher}@epfl.ch francesco.locatello@ista.ac.at
arxiv-2310-18123.description: Abstract This paper provides statistical sample complexity bounds for score-matching and its applications in causal discovery. We demonstrate that accurate estimation of the score function is achievable by training a standard deep ReLU neural network using stochastic gradient descent. We establish bounds on the error rate of recovering causal relationships using the score-matching-based causal discovery method of Rolland et al.

arxiv-2403-09751.title: What Was Your Prompt? A Remote Keylogging Attack on AI Assistants
arxiv-2403-09751.creator: Roy Weiss , Daniel Ayzenshteyn , Guy Amit, Yisroel Mirsky
arxiv-2403-09751.description: Abstract AI assistants are becoming an integral part of society, used for asking advice or help in personal and confidential issues. In this paper, we unveil a novel side-channel that can be used to read encrypted responses from AI Assistants over the web: the token-length side-channel. We found that many vendors, including OpenAI and Microsoft, have this side-channel.

arxiv-2408-01132.title: Spectral methods on a triangle and W-systems
arxiv-2408-01132.creator: Jing Gao, Arieh Iserles
arxiv-2408-01132.description: Abstract We present an overarching framework for stable spectral methods on a triangle, defined by a multivariate W-system and based on orthogonal polynomials on the triangle. Motivated by the Koornwinder orthogonal polynomials on the triangle, we introduce a Koornwinder W-system.

arxiv-2504-16887.title: The Sponge is Quantum Indifferentiable
arxiv-2504-16887.creator: Gorjan Alagic, Joseph Carolan, Christian Majenz, Saliha Tokat
arxiv-2504-16887.description: Abstract The sponge is a cryptographic construction that turns a public permutation into a hash function. When instantiated with the Keccak permutation, the sponge forms the NIST SHA-3 standard. SHA-3 is a core component of most post-quantum public-key cryptography schemes slated for worldwide adoption.

arxiv-2506-05333.title: Kinetics: Rethinking Test-Time Scaling Laws
arxiv-2506-05333.creator: Ranajoy Sadhukhan ∗, Zhuoming Chen ∗, Haizhong Zheng, Yang Zhou, Emma Strubell, Beidi Chen
arxiv-2506-05333.description: Abstract We rethink test-time scaling laws from a practical efficiency perspective, revealing that the effectiveness of smaller models is significantly overestimated. Prior work, grounded in compute-optimality, overlooks critical memory access bottlenecks introduced by inference-time strategies (e.g., Best-of- N N , long CoTs). arxiv-2507-05233.title: Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Dissipative Nano-Optics and Magnetodielectric Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
arxiv-2507-05233.creator: Lars Meschede, Daniel D. A. Clarke, Ortwin Hess
arxiv-2507-05233.description: Abstract The unprecedented pace of evolution in nanoscale architectures for cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) has posed crucial challenges for theory, where the quantum dynamics arising from the non-perturbative dressing of matter by cavity electric and magnetic fields, as well as the fundamentally non-hermitian character of the system are to be treated without significant approximation.

arxiv-2507-16422.title: Effective sample size estimation based on concordance between p p -value and posterior probability of the null hypothesis
arxiv-2507-16422.creator: Han Wang, Yan Dora Zhang, Guosheng Yin
arxiv-2507-16422.description: Abstract Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) of a prior distribution is an age-old yet pivotal challenge, with great implications for clinical trials and various biomedical applications. Although numerous endeavors have been dedicated to this pursuit, most of them neglect the likelihood context in which the prior is embedded, thereby considering all priors as “beneficial”.

pmc-10603147.title: Evidence of unconventional superconductivity on the surface of the nodal semimetal CaAg1−xPdxP
pmc-10603147.creator: Rikizo Yano, Shota Nagasaka, Naoki Matsubara, Kazushige Saigusa, Tsuyoshi Tanda, Seiichiro Ito, Ai Yamakage, Yoshihiko Okamoto, Koshi Takenaka, Satoshi Kashiwaya
pmc-10603147.description: Surface states of topological materials provide extreme electronic states for unconventional superconducting states. CaAg1−xPdxP is an ideal candidate for a nodal-line Dirac semimetal with drumhead surface states and no additional bulk bands. Here, we report that CaAg1−xPdxP has surface states that exhibit unconventional superconductivity (SC) around 1.5 K.

pmc-10804104.title: Quality specification of ice creams produced with different homofermentative lactic acid bacteria
pmc-10804104.creator: Gökhan Akarca, Mehmet Kilinç, Ayşe Janseli Denizkara
pmc-10804104.description: This study investigated the changes in the physicochemical, microbiological, textural, and nutritional values of ice cream produced by various methods with the addition of different lactic acid bacteria. Adding lactic acid bacteria to the ice cream mix caused a decrease in firmness, consistency, cohesiveness, index of viscosity, pH, aw, first drop, complete melting, and overrun values (p < .05).

pmc-11471336.title: The Influence of Family Adversities on Longitudinal Changes in Physical Inactivity Among Korean Adolescents During the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-11471336.creator: Tae Kyoung Lee, Jing Zhu, Young Mi Kim, Ze-Kai Jiang, Meilin Zhang, Won Ha Choi, Tae-Young Pak, Hana Song
pmc-11471336.description: Objectives:Lack of physical activity has a critical effect on the physical and mental health of adolescents. This study examined the influence of family adversities on the longitudinal changes in physical inactivity among adolescents during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.Methods:The study used multi-wave data from the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey, including 2590 Korean adolescents aged 12-14 years.

pmc-11654216.title: The anesthesiologist’s guide to critically assessing machine learning research: a narrative review
pmc-11654216.creator: Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Sergio Alzate-Ricaurte, Tomas Eduardo Mejia Vallecilla, Gustavo Adolfo Cruz-Suarez
pmc-11654216.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially Machine Learning (ML), has developed systems capable of performing tasks that require human intelligence. In anesthesiology and other medical fields, AI applications can improve the precision and efficiency of daily clinical practice, and can also facilitate a personalized approach to patient care, which can lead to improved outcomes and quality of care.

pmc-11692742.title: QUANTIFYING ASSOCIATIVE AND ATTENTIONAL INFLUENCES ON MEMORY FOR EVENTS
pmc-11692742.creator: Alan Kersten, Kevin Darby, Megan Smithwick, Julie Earles
pmc-11692742.description: Aging is associated with declines in multiple aspects of the human memory system, including hippocampally-mediated associative abilities and frontally-mediated executive abilities. It is important to distinguish these different impacts of aging in order to identify possible causes of memory decline (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease vs. vascular dementia).

pmc-11699628.title: An oncolytic HAdV-5 with reduced surface charge combines diminished toxicity and improved tumor targeting
pmc-11699628.creator: Frederik Wienen, Robin Nilson, Ellen Allmendinger, Sarah Peters, Thomas FE Barth, Stefan Kochanek, Lea Krutzke
pmc-11699628.description: Human adenovirus type 5 (HAdV-5)-based oncolytic viruses hold significant promise for anti-cancer therapy. However, poor tumor-targeting and off-target organ transduction after systemic administration limit their therapeutic efficacy. In addition, the strong liver tropism of HAdV-5-based vectors poses the risk of hepatotoxicity.

pmc-12436451.title: Comparative study of functional training and traditional resistance training on lower-limb strength performance in male adolescent volleyball players: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12436451.creator: Yuan Gao, Yale Yang, Chenyang Xian, Zetao Wang
pmc-12436451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the effects of a functional strength-training program designed around volleyball-specific movements with those of traditional resistance training on lower-limb performance in male adolescent volleyball players.MethodsIn a randomized controlled trial, 52 male volleyball athletes (age 13 ± 2 years; ≥2 years of formal volleyball training) from a sports school in Huangshi, Hubei Province, China, were allocated 1:1 to a functional training group (n = 26) or a traditional resistance training group (n = 26).

pmc-12654211.title: SAW-Based Hydrogen Sensing: Mechanisms, Design Strategies, and Future Prospects
pmc-12654211.creator: Shengzhuo Chen, Jin Chai, Libo Gao, Rongjie Wang, Zhonggang Zhang, Ziming Ren, Hongyan Xu, Yihui Lan, Kezhen Ma, Meng Li
pmc-12654211.description: Hydrogen is widely considered a clean and sustainable energy carrier due to its high energy density, abundant reserves, and zero carbon emissions during use. To ensure safety in hydrogen production, transportation, and utilization, the development of high-performance hydrogen sensors is of great importance.

pmc-12656587.title: Dengue Fever Resurgence in Iran: An Integrative Review of Causative Factors and Control Strategies
pmc-12656587.creator: Seyed Hassan Nikookar, Saeedeh Hoseini, Omid Dehghan, Mahmoud Fazelidinan, Ahmadali Enayati
pmc-12656587.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Dengue fever, a mosquito-borne viral disease, has become a significant global health concern in recent decades, particularly in Iran. This integrative review provides a comprehensive assessment of the epidemiological trends of dengue fever in Iran from its initial emergence to the present, identifying and evaluating factors contributing to both the emergence and re-emergence of the disease at national and international levels.

pmc-12734940.title: Mechanical Response and Parameter Sensitivity of Flexible Membrane Sealed Caverns for Compressed Air Energy Storage
pmc-12734940.creator: Lihua Hu, Jihan Liu, Zhixu Guo, Xin Liang, Liyuan Yu, Wei Li, Chengguo Hu, Yun Wu, Shihao Guo, Xuanyuan Liu, Qiming Zhou
pmc-12734940.description: Implementing compressed air energy storage (CAES) in lined caverns provides a promising technical solution for large-scale energy storage, and the reasonable selection of sealing materials is essential for its success. Flexible membrane materials including sprayable polymers, rubber sheets, and airbags have recently been considered economical and practical sealing options.

pmc-13050263.title: Spatial resolution of exposure to particulate matter (PM2.5) and the impact on the burden of disease in Germany
pmc-13050263.creator: Stefan Wallek, Marcel Langner, Dietrich Plass, Sarah Kienzler, Tobias Sauter
pmc-13050263.description: Accurate estimation of the disease burden attributable to ambient particulate matter (PM2.5) requires reliable exposure data with an adequate spatial resolution. While coarse-resolution models are commonly used for national assessments, the impact of spatial resolution on environmental burden of disease (EBD) estimates remains understudied. We compared two modelling approaches for PM2.

pmc-13326252.title: Filamin C Genetic Cardiomyopathy Presenting as Acute Myocardial Injury
pmc-13326252.creator: Francisco B Alexandrino, Brett Curtis, Christopher Nguyen, Deborah Kwon, Jay Ramchand, WH Wilson Tang
pmc-13326252.description: BackgroundAcute myocardial injury with a nonischemic imaging pattern presents a diagnostic challenge.Case SummaryA 46-year-old previously healthy man presented with intermittent chest pain and markedly elevated high-sensitivity troponin. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed extensive ring-like subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement involving 10 left ventricular segments but no myocardial edema. Genetic testing subsequently identified a pathogenic variant in the FLNC gene.

pmc-13576343.title: Predictive value of the novel cardiometabolic index for reduced aerobic capacity in patients with coronary heart disease: a clinical comparative study of 378 cases
pmc-13576343.creator: He Huang, Jiangwei Ma, Gaonian Zhao, Su Jiang
pmc-13576343.description: BackgroundCoronary heart disease(CHD) is an important cause of cardiovascular diseases and, under adverse conditions such as arteriosclerosis, will raise the risk of death significantly. Due to the shortcomings of traditional adiposity indices when assessing aerobic capacity (AC), this paper intended to explore whether the novel cardiometabolic index (CMI) could predict lower AC in patients with coronary heart disease.

uslaw-usc-t46-s7306.title: 46 U.S.C. § 7306 — General requirements and classifications for members of deck departments
uslaw-usc-t46-s7306.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s7306.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part E (Merchant Seamen Licenses, Certificates, And Documents); Chapter 73 (Merchant Mariners’ Documents). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— The Secretary may issue a merchant mariner credential, to members of the deck department in the following classes: (1) Able Seaman-Unlimited. (2) Able Seaman-Limited. (3) Able Seaman-Special. (4) Able Seaman-Offshore Supply Vessels. (5) Able Seaman-Sail.
